focus: Model lifecycle transitions explicitly from initialization through readiness, work, drain, close, failure, and recovery.
Distinguish observed readiness from internal acknowledgement and reject path existence or process liveness as sufficient proof.
Attack race windows, partial cleanup, orphaned resources, unsafe retry, and false success after asynchronous work.
Keep lifecycle observations and recovery advice separate from process control, deployment, approval, or merge authority.
Require deterministic transition evidence, bounded timeouts, platform-aware behavior, and reproducible recovery tests.
